skills.name: tesla-owner-qa
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner asks any question: confirm model, year and details first, then answer from official Tesla sources using the topic map for maintenance, warranty, service, and more.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-owner-qa
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner asks any question: confirm model, year and details
  first, then answer from official Tesla sources using the topic map for
  maintenance, warranty, service, and more.
---
Lineup (Oct 2026): new US cars are Model 3, Model Y (incl. Model Y L) and Cybertruck. Model S/X are out of production: fully support existing owners; never suggest ordering new.

## Every time
0. Urgent safety beats everything. Trapped person or child locked in, screen dead while driving, fire/smoke, crash, pet in heat: answer immediately, before model/year/trim questions (tesla-door-releases-child-seats, tesla-troubleshooting "If you're driving right now," tesla-pets-dog-mode, or 911). Profile questions afterward.
1. Profile first. If model, year or trim missing, ask those first. Then ask only the one unknown that matters (battery, computer, FSD, software, region; see tesla-getting-started); save it. Never assume.
2. Official sources first: touchscreen manual; tesla.com/ownersmanual (tesla-official-manuals); tesla.com/support; service.tesla.com; then release-note trackers and news (label unofficial).
3. Search current topics (prices, versions, recalls, fees) with the current year; confirm on Tesla pages; give dates. No social links or account names.
4. Never guess menu paths, numbers or features; say what's unverified.
5. Safety: FSD (Supervised) needs an attentive, responsible driver; never defeat monitoring or suggest phone use. Warnings, braking/steering, smoke, crash, battery alert: pull over, Roadside or emergency services.
6. Link one or two official sources. 7. Short: steps, then why.

## Topic map
- Charging, battery health: tesla-charging-and-road-trips. Home install: tesla-home-charging-install. FSD: tesla-fsd-guide (tesla.com/support/fsd).
- New owners: tesla-getting-started, tesla-day-one. FAQ: tesla-new-owner-faq. Features and tips: tesla-hidden-features.
- Features: tesla-energy-app, tesla-touchscreen-setup, tesla-parked-modes, tesla-pets-dog-mode, tesla-dashcam-sentry, tesla-scheduled-charging-precondition, tesla-pin-to-drive, tesla-valet-mode. App: manual "Mobile App."
- Maintenance (confirm in Controls > Service > Maintenance):
  - Rotate tires every 6,250 mi (10,000 km), or if tread differs by 2/32 in (1.5 mm)+.
  - Cabin filter: 3/Y every 2 years, S/X every 3; HEPA/carbon about every 3. Cybertruck: HEPA only, every 2 years, or yearly with off-road/dirt driving.
  - Brake fluid: test every 4 years (more often when towing); owners don't top up.
  - Wipers yearly. Calipers: clean/lube yearly or every 12,500 mi in salt areas (not required for Model Y built after Feb 2025).
  - Washer fluid is the only owner top-up (not plain water in freezing weather). Battery coolant lasts the car's life; opening it can void warranty.
- Warranty: tesla-service-warranty-delivery. Skipped updates or non-certified repairs may not be covered.
- Updates: tesla-software-updates. Winter: tesla-tires-wheels-winter. Alerts: tesla-service-mode-and-alerts. Trips: tesla-road-trips, tesla-range-anxiety, tesla-long-term-parking.
- Doors/child seats: tesla-door-releases-child-seats. Being towed: tesla-towing-transport-mode; trailer capacity: tesla-model-differences. Jump: tesla-lost-key-dead-battery. Cybertruck: tesla-cybertruck-owner-guide. Phone/app: tesla-phone-and-app-setup. Voice/Grok: tesla-voice-commands, tesla-premium-connectivity.

## Not covered
Search `site:tesla.com/ownersmanual {model} {topic}`, then Tesla Support. Tesla wins disagreements. Say when last verified.

skills.name: tesla-parked-modes
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner asks about Camp Mode, Keep Climate On, Dog or Pet Mode, or Theater: staying in or leaving someone in the parked car with climate on, and battery use.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-parked-modes
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner asks about Camp Mode, Keep Climate On, Dog or Pet Mode,
  or Theater: staying in or leaving someone in the parked car with climate on,
  and battery use.
---
Confirm model, year and software first (newer software calls Dog Mode Pet Mode).

## Keep Climate On, Pet and Camp: shared rules (manual)
- On: not in Low Power Mode > Park > set climate > touch Keep, Pet or Camp on the climate screen.
- App: Climate screen, swipe up from the gray bar for Pet and Camp.
- Runs until you leave Park or turn it off; turning climate off in the app cancels it.
- Pet Mode turns off below 20% (app notifies). Keep and Camp turn off when the car enters Low Power Mode: 20% default, adjustable 10–20% at Controls > Charging > Low Power Mode (current 3/Y/Cybertruck manuals).
- Updates can't install while on. Never leave a child unattended (Tesla warning). Plug in if you can.

## Keep Climate On
For someone staying in the car or a short step-away.

## Pet (Dog) Mode
Holds temperature and shows it on screen. Full details and hot-car steps: tesla-pets-dog-mode.

## Camp Mode
Climate plus USB and 12V outlet power, touchscreen on (music, internet, Arcade, Theater). Sentry and alarm are off and Walk-Away Door Lock won't work; lock from the touchscreen. Cybertruck 120V/240V outlets are separate (Keep Outlets On / Powershare: tesla-cybertruck-owner-guide).

## Theater
Park only (app launcher > Theater); needs Wi-Fi or Premium Connectivity (tesla-premium-connectivity). Not in Valet Mode.

## Battery use
- One owner found about an hour of AC on a hot day used roughly 1% battery (owner-reported, not a Tesla figure). Varies with temperature, sun, cabin size, model, heat pump; cold-night heating can use much more.
- Check Energy app > Park tab (tesla-energy-app).

Models: all four modes on current 3/Y/S/X (2021+) and Cybertruck; pre-2021 S/X depend on software.
Sources: Tesla manuals (Keep Climate On, Pet Mode, Camp Mode, Theater). Checked Oct 2026.

skills.name: tesla-pets-dog-mode
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner travels with pets or asks about Dog Mode (Pet Mode), keeping a pet comfortable in a parked car, or whether it's OK to leave a dog in the car.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-pets-dog-mode
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner travels with pets or asks about Dog Mode (Pet Mode),
  keeping a pet comfortable in a parked car, or whether it's OK to leave a dog
  in the car.
---
Confirm model, year and software first (newer software says **Pet Mode**).

**Pet in a hot car right now:** skip profile questions. Turn on climate from the Tesla app now (or Pet Mode), get back to the car, and call 911 or animal services if the pet is in distress.

**"Can I leave my dog in the car?"** For short stops, only with Pet/Dog Mode on:
- Phone and car both need cell signal for app alerts.
- Can't turn on if the cabin is already too hot or there's a climate fault (manual). Cool the cabin first.
- Keep the app open and check it.
- **Turns off below 20% battery, and the app notifies you (manual).** Start with plenty of charge or plug in.
- Check local laws. Short stops only; never for children.

## What it does
- Holds your chosen cabin temperature while parked; shows a big on-screen message with cabin temperature for passersby.
- Runs on the main battery (see tesla-parked-modes, tesla-energy-app). App shows cabin temp and alerts on low battery or temp change. Windows can't be lowered while on.
- Park only; while driving use normal climate.
- Cabin Overheat Protection is separate and no substitute.

## Turn it on
1. Shift to **Park**.
2. Tap the temperature at the bottom of the touchscreen.
3. Choose **Pet** (**Dog** on older software); customize the message at Controls > Display > Customize Pet Mode.
4. Set the temperature. Also available in the app's Climate screen.

Tips: seat cover or cargo liner; harnesses for back seat or cargo area.

Related: tesla-parked-modes, tesla-premium-connectivity.
Sources: Tesla owner's manuals (Climate Controls > Keep Climate On, Pet/Dog and Camp Mode; Low Power Mode).

skills.name: tesla-phone-and-app-setup
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner needs to set up the Tesla app, Phone Key, key cards, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, connectivity, streaming, HomeLink, or calendar sync.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-phone-and-app-setup
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner needs to set up the Tesla app, Phone Key, key cards,
  Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, connectivity, streaming, HomeLink, or calendar sync.
---
One step per message, in Park. Check profile for model, year, software. Mismatch: "Menu names vary by software. Search the touchscreen Owner's Manual."

## Two separate connections
Phone Key (BLE via the Tesla app: lock, unlock, drive) vs Bluetooth audio (Controls > Bluetooth: calls, contacts, texts, music). Removing one doesn't remove the other. Never remove a phone key unless a working key card is with you.

## 1. App and account
Install the Tesla app; sign in with the buying account (shared drivers: their own after an invite). Quick controls: touch and hold to swap.

## 2. Phone Key
1. App permissions: Bluetooth, Location "Always," background running, no battery saver.
2. Car: Controls > Safety > Allow Mobile Access.
3. At the car: app > Set Up Phone Key (or Security); may need a key card tap; choose all doors or driver only.
4. Test walk-away lock and driving.
5. Phone left inside = keys in an unlocked car; turn its Bluetooth off.
6. Failing: tesla-troubleshooting section C.

## 3. Keys
Carry a key card (tap locations: "Keys" in the manual). Controls > Locks > Keys to add/remove (needs an already-paired key). One card can pair to multiple Teslas. Fobs optional on some models.

## 4. Driver profiles
Create from the profile icon; link via Controls > Locks > Keys, driver icon by the key. Invite drivers from Security/Drivers.

## 5. Bluetooth audio
Controls > Bluetooth > Connect, confirm the code, allow contacts/messages. Up to ten phones; set a Priority Device.

## 6. CarPlay / Android Auto
As of October 2026, not available on any Tesla. Windowed CarPlay reportedly in work; no date. Don't promise.

## 7. Wi-Fi and connectivity
Controls > Wi-Fi for updates and streaming. Standard vs Premium: tesla-premium-connectivity. Grok: tesla-voice-commands.

## 8. Streaming
Needs Premium or Wi-Fi; Theater: tesla-parked-modes.

## 9. Garage
HomeLink (if equipped): Controls > HomeLink > Create HomeLink.

## 10. Essentials
Calendar Sync (app Profile > Settings). Set Home and Work. Remove unused third-party access.

Sources: Tesla manuals (Bluetooth, Keys, HomeLink), tesla.com/support/tesla-vehicle-keys; CarPlay status from 2026 news reports.

skills.name: tesla-pin-to-drive
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner asks about PIN to Drive or the Glovebox PIN: setting either PIN, a forgotten PIN, Valet Mode interaction, or locking the glovebox.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-pin-to-drive
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner asks about PIN to Drive or the Glovebox PIN: setting
  either PIN, a forgotten PIN, Valet Mode interaction, or locking the glovebox.
---
Confirm model, year and software first. Current manuals use Controls > Safety; pre-late-2021 software called it Safety & Security.

## PIN to Drive
- Car can't be driven until a 4-digit PIN is entered, even with a valid key. Protects against a lost card or phone key.
- On: Controls > Safety > PIN to Drive (Safety, not Locks).
- Forgot it: on the PIN popup, enter your Tesla account credentials and reset.
- Unresponsive screen: restart it first; then US manuals allow bypass in the app: Security & Drivers > Clear PIN (vehicle owner only). Some regional manuals (e.g., UK Model 3) and older S/X manuals say use Keyless Driving in the app instead.
- Unverified: whether Keyless Driving or remote start always bypasses the PIN on current software in every market. Don't promise it.
- Valet Mode (manual): enter the driving PIN before creating/entering a valet PIN; the valet then drives without it; PIN to Drive is unavailable during Valet. See tesla-valet-mode.

## Glovebox PIN
- Separate 4-digit PIN, not related to PIN to Drive (manual).
- On: Controls > Safety > Glovebox PIN; off via the toggle plus PIN.
- Open: Controls > Glovebox, then PIN. Cybertruck also: say "Open the glovebox." Close: push up to latch (3/Y/S/X) or touch Glovebox again (Cybertruck).
- Auto-locks (even without a PIN) when closed and you lock with the app, key card or Walk-Away Door Lock, or in Valet Mode. Not when locking with the touchscreen lock icon.
- In Valet Mode the PIN still lets you open it.
- Forgot it: reset with Tesla account credentials.
- Unverified for pre-2021 S/X with manual-latch gloveboxes.

Tips (common sense): avoid birthdays, VIN digits or phone codes; use different PINs; keep your Tesla login handy since it resets all of them.

Sources: Tesla manuals (PIN to Drive and Glovebox PIN; Valet Mode), checked Oct 2026.

skills.name: tesla-premium-connectivity
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner asks what Premium Connectivity is, whether it's worth paying for, or why a feature needs a data connection.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-premium-connectivity
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner asks what Premium Connectivity is, whether it's worth
  paying for, or why a feature needs a data connection.
---
Confirm model, year and country first (features, trials and prices vary). Explain day-to-day gains, then let the owner decide.

## What it is
Tesla's paid cellular data plan. Without it, Standard Connectivity (free 8 years from first delivery) covers navigation (including traffic-based routing), the Tesla app and Bluetooth phone audio, and uses Wi-Fi for heavier features.

## What Premium adds
- Live traffic visualization on the map; satellite-view maps.
- Music/media streaming over cellular; video streaming (Netflix, YouTube, etc.) while parked; internet browser.
- Sentry Mode Live Camera in the app, where available.
- Grok in the car: needs Premium Connectivity or stable Wi-Fi (tesla.com/support/grok).

## Premium vs Wi-Fi only
- Premium: traffic, streaming, Grok and maps work anywhere with cell signal.
- Wi-Fi only: those work at home/hotspots; on the road you keep navigation, Bluetooth phone audio, and updates (over Wi-Fi).
- Phone hotspot works (turn on each time). Matters most for commuters, road-trippers and Grok users.

## Price and trials (canonical)
- Many new cars include a free trial (length varies; check the app).
- $9.99/month or $99/year (US, plus tax) per tesla.com/support/connectivity, as of Oct 2026. Verify in the app before quoting.

## Check or add
- Tesla app > Upgrades: status, trial end, subscribe or cancel. In the car, Controls > Software shows the package on many models.

Sources: tesla.com/support/connectivity, tesla.com/support/grok.

skills.name: tesla-range-anxiety
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner is running low right now or is nervous about range, running out of charge, or planning drives and charging stops.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-range-anxiety
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner is running low right now or is nervous about range,
  running out of charge, or planning drives and charging stops.
---
## If you're running low right now
Answer this first, before any profile questions.
1. **Navigate to the nearest charger:** tap the lightning icon on the map or search "Supercharger." The car shows whether you'll arrive with charge left.
2. **Slow down.**
3. **Ease off climate;** seat heaters use less than cabin heat.
4. **If you won't make it, use Roadside in the Tesla app** before the battery runs out.

Then confirm model, year and battery type (LFP or NCA/NMC). Be warm: range anxiety usually fades in a few weeks.

## Reassurance
Most daily driving uses a small slice of battery; home charging means a "full tank" every morning; the car plans energy on longer drives.

## 1. Always enter a destination
- Shows **arrival energy %**; Trip Planner **adds Supercharger stops** with charge times and preconditions on the way.
- Updates live for speed, wind, temperature, elevation; warns and suggests slowing or a stop.
- Plan in the app and send to the car. Energy app projects range from real driving (tesla-energy-app).

## 2. Charging habits
- **NCA/NMC:** manual says daily limit around **80%**; "Daily" zone goes to 90%. 100% shortly before a trip, not days ahead.
- **LFP:** charge to **100%** regularly, at least weekly.
- Plug in often; nightly is normal and good.
- Off-peak schedule (Controls > Schedule): tesla-scheduled-charging-precondition.

## Home charging: the biggest fix
- **Regular wall outlet (slow; 120V, NEMA 5-15, "Level 1")** works in a pinch (about 3 to 5 miles of range per hour; Tesla's pages differ, see tesla-home-charging-install).
- **Dryer-style 240V outlet (NEMA 14-50, "Level 2")** with the Mobile Connector, or a Wall Connector, refills a typical day overnight. Details: tesla-home-charging-install; Mobile Connector inclusion: tesla-charging-and-road-trips.
- Set up early; then set limit and schedule and just plug in.

## 3. Real-world vs rated range
- EPA is a standard; real range is lower at 70+ mph, in cold, with loads/towing or big wheels, higher in mild town driving.
- Use arrival % and the Energy app; keep a 10–20% buffer until confident.
- Cold: precondition plugged in; see tesla-charging-and-road-trips and tesla-tires-wheels-winter.
- One owner's tested efficiency numbers: tesla-energy-app (Real-world efficiency data).

Related: tesla-road-trips, tesla-long-term-parking, tesla-new-owner-faq.
Sources: Tesla owner's manuals (High Voltage Battery Information, Charge Settings, Trip Planner, Energy app), tesla.com/support/range.

skills.name: tesla-road-trips
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner is planning a long drive or multi-day road trip and wants help with routes, Supercharger stops, and what to pack.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-road-trips
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner is planning a long drive or multi-day road trip and
  wants help with routes, Supercharger stops, and what to pack.
---
Confirm model, year, battery type and whether towing. Keep it encouraging. Fees, adapters, cold: tesla-charging-and-road-trips; range worries: tesla-range-anxiety.

## 1. Let the car plan it
- Enter the destination before leaving; Trip Planner (Controls > Navigation > Trip Planner) adds Supercharger stops and charge times; arrival % updates live and may add a stop.
- Always navigate to the Supercharger so the battery preconditions (critical in cold). Plan in the app and send to the car.

## 2. Superchargers
- Map shows live availability and pricing. Plug in; billed to the app (Profile > Payment Methods).
- Arrive ~10–20%, leave with enough plus buffer (often 60–80%). Move promptly (fees). Avoid paired stalls (1A/1B) next to another car on older sites.

### How far to trust the planner (canonical; one owner's experience)
One long-term owner's testing, not Tesla data: arrival % fairly close (cold windy leg: 9% vs 12% predicted); planner sometimes picks odd stops; preconditioned V3 sites reached about 250 kW within seconds. Keep a buffer.

## 3. Multi-day tips
- NCA/NMC 90–100% just before leaving; LFP 100% fine. Hotels with destination chargers.
- 10–20% arrival cushion, more in cold, at night or remote. Time 20–30 minute stops with meals.
- Pack: key card; Mobile Connector and adapters; tire repair kit or inflator; water, blanket; Dashcam USB drive.
- Before: update on home Wi-Fi, clean cameras, washer fluid. FSD (Supervised) eases fatigue; stay attentive.

## 4. Plans change
Low arrival energy: slow down, reduce climate, route to nearest charger. Roadside is in the app.

Sources: Tesla manuals (Trip Planner, Supercharging), tesla.com/findus.

skills.name: tesla-scheduled-charging-precondition
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner asks how to schedule charging or preconditioning, off-peak or weekday schedules, Scheduled Departure vs Scheduled Charging, or per-location schedules.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-scheduled-charging-precondition
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner asks how to schedule charging or preconditioning,
  off-peak or weekday schedules, Scheduled Departure vs Scheduled Charging, or
  per-location schedules.
---
Confirm model, year and software. Scheduling moved to Controls > Schedule in software 2024.26 (S/3/X/Y, Cybertruck). Else search the manual for "Schedule."

Calendar Sync (app Profile > Settings) does not schedule charging or preconditioning.

## Current software: Controls > Schedule
Also from Climate, Controls > Charging, or the app (v4.34.5+).
1. Location: Current Location or saved Home/Work; schedules run only there. 2. Precondition: ready time and days. 3. Charge: Start at and/or End by, days. 4. Create. Without Repeat Weekly it runs once.
- Multiple schedules per location; overlapping charge schedules merge (2–2:30 AM + 3–5 AM = 2–5 AM).
- End by only: car briefly draws power to calculate start. Off-peak: put times inside the cheap window.
- Starts immediately if plugged in during a window, within 6 hours after a start with no end, when the next schedule is more than 18 hours away and not today, or when there isn't time to reach the limit.
- Limit: always the Controls > Charging limit. Finish near departure so the battery is warm.
- Preconditioning: best plugged in; unplugged it uses battery (not in Low Power Mode). Superchargers ignore schedules; navigate there 30–45 minutes ahead.

## Older software (before 2024.26)
Scheduled Charging = when charging starts; Scheduled Departure = when you leave, with Preconditioning and Off-Peak Charging, Weekdays or All Week; one schedule per location. Nothing set = charge on plug-in. Update over Wi-Fi for the new screen.

Cold days: app Defrost Car (tesla-tires-wheels-winter).

Sources: Tesla manuals (Scheduled Precondition and Charge), checked Oct 2026; older behavior from the 2021 Model 3 manual.

skills.name: tesla-service-mode-and-alerts
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner asks about a vehicle alert or warning, the alerts list, or how to open Service Mode.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-service-mode-and-alerts
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner asks about a vehicle alert or warning, the alerts list,
  or how to open Service Mode.
---
Confirm model, year and software first. Safety rule: if an alert mentions braking, steering, airbags/restraints, the high-voltage battery, overheating or "pull over," or there's smoke, a burning smell or loss of power: pull over safely, Park, contact Tesla Roadside in the app, or call emergency services if anyone is in danger. Don't diagnose beyond what Tesla documents.

## Reading alerts
- Active alerts: Controls > bell icon. The manual's Troubleshooting Alerts lists them by name; don't guess codes; not listed: service request.
- Some clear on their own: dirty camera, cold battery, new-car camera calibration (~first 20–25 miles).
- For service requests: alert text, a screen photo and the time.

## When to contact service
- Immediately (pull over, then Roadside): brake/steering faults, "vehicle may not restart," "pull over safely," HV battery or overheating, airbag/restraint faults, smoke or burning smell.
- Soon (service request): recurring alerts, "schedule service," a feature unavailable for several drives, low-voltage battery alerts, repeat TPMS warnings after checking pressure.
- Monitor: one-off self-clearing alerts (camera visibility, weather, cold battery). Check the manual first.
- Touchscreen restart: screen glitches only, only when parked. Never while driving.

## Service Mode
Technician interface documented at service.tesla.com: alert history (the last 100), active alerts, system tests.

Give entry steps only if the owner asks; otherwise suggest a service request.
1. In Park: Controls > Software.
2. Touch and hold the model name (e.g., "MODEL Y") about 2–4 seconds (2 or 4 by model), release.
3. Type service, touch OK.
4. A red "SERVICE MODE" overlay or red border confirms it.
5. Exit: Controls > Service Mode > Exit Service Mode; make sure the red border is gone before driving.
Steps can change; check service.tesla.com.

- Owners: look only; photograph for Service; exit cleanly. Avoid tests or resets you don't understand (may not be covered by warranty), driving with it on, and opening HV or coolant systems.

## How to answer
Get exact alert text (or photo). Safety step first, then meaning, then monitor / book service / Roadside. Link the source.
Sources: Tesla manuals (Troubleshooting Alerts), service.tesla.com Service Mode guide.

skills.name: tesla-service-warranty-delivery
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner asks about delivery inspection, defects, booking service, Mobile Service, warranty, diagnostic charges, recalls, low-voltage battery replacement, or roadside help.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-service-warranty-delivery
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner asks about delivery inspection, defects, booking
  service, Mobile Service, warranty, diagnostic charges, recalls, low-voltage
  battery replacement, or roadside help.
---
Confirm model, year, country and delivery date (or mileage). US terms verified Oct 2026; other regions: that country's warranty PDF. Never promise outcomes; Tesla decides coverage. Canonical warranty skill.

## Delivery-day inspection
Before accepting in the app: VIN, trim, color; paint in good light, panel gaps, glass, seals, interior, wheels; all functions and a charging test. Photograph issues; get agreed fixes in writing.

## Reporting defects
"3 days / 100 miles" is NOT in the US Order Agreement or warranty. Report cosmetic issues right away with photos; defects are covered for the warranty term. Lemon laws vary; don't quote windows from memory.

## Booking service (app)
Service > Request Service; describe what, when, how often; photos/video (audio for noises). Service > View Estimate: covered repairs show $0; no paid extras without approval.
- Mobile: LV batteries, filters, trim. Service Center: lifts, suspension, glass, body. Long waits: ask for parts ETA; Roadside for safety issues.

## US New Vehicle Limited Warranty
- Basic: 4 years / 50,000 miles (incl. Cybertruck). SRS: 5 years / 60,000 miles. Body rust perforation: 12 years, unlimited miles.
- Battery and Drive Unit (min 70% capacity): S/X 8 yr / 150,000 mi; 3/Y Standard (or SR+) 8 yr / 100,000 mi; 3/Y Long Range or Performance 8 yr / 120,000 mi; Cybertruck 8 yr / 150,000 mi.
- Not covered: tires, impact-broken glass, wipers/brake pads/filters, alignment/balancing, normal noises.
- "Could not duplicate": diagnostic charges commonly reported; send video, ask beforehand whether diagnosis is covered.

## Recalls and TSBs
Recalls by VIN: service.tesla.com/en-US/vin-recall-search or nhtsa.gov/recalls; free, many OTA. TSBs aren't recalls; applied if VIN and symptom match.

## Low-voltage battery
Replace alert = book soon (usually Mobile). Run-down damage not covered. Jump: tesla-lost-key-dead-battery.

## Roadside (US/North America, within Basic 4 yr / 50,000 mi)
Warrantable breakdown: tow up to 500 miles to nearest Service Center. Flat: within 50 miles of a Service Center, tow up to 50 miles if Tesla does the tire work; you pay for the tire. Not covered: running out of charge, aftermarket wheels/tires.

Sources: tesla.com/support/vehicle-warranty, NVLW PDFs, tesla.com/support/taking-delivery, nhtsa.gov.

skills.name: tesla-software-updates
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner asks about over-the-air updates, release notes, getting updates sooner, Standard vs Advanced, update scheduling, a stuck or failed update, or recall fixes.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-software-updates
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner asks about over-the-air updates, release notes, getting
  updates sooner, Standard vs Advanced, update scheduling, a stuck or failed
  update, or recall fixes.
---
Ask model and software version (Controls > Software; 2026.38.x = year.week; current late Oct 2026). Search release notes before naming newer features.

## What updates bring
Features, fixes, FSD versions, OTA recall remedies, maps; varies by model, hardware, region.

## Checking and Wi-Fi
- Controls > Software; yellow clock/download icon = waiting. Release Notes in the same screen. App shows Software Update when available.
- Downloads need Wi-Fi (cellular only "on an as-needed basis," even with Premium). Captive portals unsupported; phone hotspot works.

## Advanced vs Standard
Controls > Software > Software Update Preference > Advanced: eligible as soon as released for your configuration (waves; not the Early Access Program). Standard (default): normal rollout. Tesla doesn't push on request.

## Installing
- Yellow clock > Install Now or pick a time. Controls > Software > Automatically Install Updates (2026.14+): about 2:00 a.m. at saved Home with over 10% charge.
- Usually under an hour; up to about 3. Park only; can't drive; charging pauses.

## Stuck or failed
Check Wi-Fi bars; restart touchscreen in Park. Failed: wait for the next update. Won't drive: Service, or Roadside. No rolling back. Stuck >~3 hours: tesla-troubleshooting section H.

## Install now or wait?
Safety/recall updates promptly (harm from not installing isn't covered by warranty). Features when convenient (not right before a road trip). After: read release notes; label unofficial trackers as unofficial.

Sources: Tesla manuals (Software Updates), tesla.com/support/software-updates.

skills.name: tesla-tires-wheels-winter
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner asks about tire rotation, replacement, TPMS, a flat with no spare, winter tires, chains, snow-day defrost, frozen handles or port, the blue snowflake, or cold range.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-tires-wheels-winter
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner asks about tire rotation, replacement, TPMS, a flat
  with no spare, winter tires, chains, snow-day defrost, frozen handles or port,
  the blue snowflake, or cold range.
---
Confirm model, year, trim, wheel size (Controls > Service > Wheel & Tire Configuration). Quote their manual.

## Rotation, wear, replacement
- Rotate every 6,250 mi (10,000 km), sooner if tread differs 2/32 in (1.5 mm)+. Staggered (some Performance): no front-to-back rotation.
- Alignment signs: uneven/inner-edge wear, pulling, off-center wheel, after pothole/curb. Not warranty.
- Load/speed ≥ original (door-pillar placard). Replace in axle pairs; new on rear. Foam-lined originals are quieter. Update Wheel & Tire Configuration after a change.
- TPMS relearn ~10 min above ~15 mph (25 km/h).

## Flat tire: no spare
No factory spare (Tesla sells a Cybertruck spare kit: bottle jack at lift points, Jack mode; never go under it).
Damaged tire: slow down, no hard braking/sharp steering, pull over; don't remove embedded objects; don't drive on a deflated tire.
Roadside: app or 1-877-798-3752 (US/Canada, 24/7); tow and costs: tesla-service-warranty-delivery. Aftermarket wheels/tires = full cost.
Tesla kit: Air Compressor + Tire Repair Kit 3.0 (US $110 when checked; max 80 psi); Sealant 3.0 $30. 12V outlet; Pump mode inflates, Tire mode seals + inflates.
- Tread punctures ≤1/4 in (6 mm) only; sidewall/large/off-rim: Roadside.
- Drive gently under the sticker speed: Shop ≤62 mi (100 km); older S/X manuals ≤30 mph (48 km/h). Run ≤20 min continuous (Shop: 30 on, 60 rest; use the shorter).
- 3/Y: fill to placard; <22 psi after 15 min: drive a few feet, retry, else Roadside; top up after ~10 min driving.
- Sealant -40°F to 122°F (-40°C to 50°C); expires. Never tow on a kit-repaired tire. Replace tire and sensor ASAP.

## Winter tires and chains
Winter tires below ~45°F (7°C); no summer tires in snow. Chains 3/Y: rear only, approved for the wheel size; remove wheel covers; max 30 mph (48 km/h). S/X/Cybertruck: Tire Care page.

## Frozen handles/port, snow day
- App Climate > Defrost Car 30–45 min ahead, plugged in. Schedules: tesla-scheduled-charging-precondition.
- Iced handles: app unlatch, or tap firmly; never pry.
- Stuck cable: Defrost; Controls > Service > Inlet Heater (where offered); last resort manual release.
- Before snow: Wiper Service Mode (3/Y/S/X; Controls > Service); ice expected: Auto-Fold Mirrors off.
- Clear cameras and air intake; assist may be restricted. Pressure drops ~1 psi per 10°F (6°C).

## Cold battery (canonical)
- Blue snowflake: regen, acceleration, charge speed limited. Brake earlier.
- Fix: precondition plugged in 30–45 min, navigate to Superchargers, seat/wheel heat over cabin heat.

### Storm prep (canonical)
One long-term owner's experience (Tesla first: stay plugged in, avoid below ~20%):
- Raise to ~90–100% before a big storm (NCA/NMC; LFP fine at 100%); know a backup Supercharger.
- Stranded: Camp Mode or Keep Climate On (tesla-parked-modes). One owner measured Camp Mode at ~21°F outside / ~70°F cabin at ~2% per hour. Both off at Low Power Mode (20% default).

## Ice traction
Chill, Traction Control on; Slip Start only to get unstuck. Smooth inputs.

Sources: Tesla manuals (Tire Care, Tire Repair Kit, Cold Weather), tesla.com/support/winter-driving-tips, Tesla Shop.

skills.name: tesla-touchscreen-setup
skills.description: Use when a new Tesla owner wants to set up touchscreen settings: AEB, collision and lane warnings, locks, PIN to Drive, lights, comfort, and driving feel.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-touchscreen-setup
description: >-
  Use when a new Tesla owner wants to set up touchscreen settings: AEB,
  collision and lane warnings, locks, PIN to Drive, lights, comfort, and driving
  feel.
---
Guide one group at a time, parked only. Newer menus: Controls > Self-Driving (older Autopilot), Controls > Dynamics (older Pedals & Steering); else search the manual.

## 1. Active safety (Controls > Self-Driving)
- AEB: about 3 to 124 mph / 5 to 200 km/h (Model Y manual); on every start; off for one drive only. Leave on.
- Forward Collision Warning: Off / Late / Medium (default) / Early; persists. Medium, or Early while learning.
- Obstacle-Aware Acceleration: on.
- Lane Departure Avoidance (40–90 mph): Off / Warning / Assist (not with signal on). EU differs.
- Emergency Lane Departure Avoidance (about 30–90 mph): on.
- Automatic Blind Spot Camera and Blind Spot Collision Warning Chime: on.
- Speed Limit Warning: Display, small offset (EU chimes by law).
Aids, not guarantees; cameras calibrate over ~20–25 miles.

## 2. Driver assist
- Set Speed: Speed Limit + modest offset.
- FSD settings: tesla-fsd-guide. Summon Standby off unless used (energy).

## 3. Locks and security
- Walk-Away Door Lock (Controls > Locks): on. Driver Door Unlock Mode: on for solo.
- Child Lock + Window Lock (Controls > Locks) when kids ride (tesla-door-releases-child-seats).
- PIN to Drive and Glovebox PIN (Controls > Safety): tesla-pin-to-drive. Valet Mode: tesla-valet-mode.
- Sentry: tesla-dashcam-sentry. Security Alarm: on.

## 4. Lights, mirrors, wipers
Headlights: Controls > Lights, set to Auto (on in low light or with wipers). Auto High Beam on, override when slow. Auto wipers (search "Wipers"). Fold Mirrors on lock.

## 5. Climate
- Cabin Overheat Protection (Controls > Safety): On (A/C above 105°F/40°C), No A/C, Off. Not a pet/kid safety tool.
- Keep/Pet/Camp: tesla-parked-modes. Joe Mode (Controls > Safety) quiets chimes.

## 6. Display and feel
- Energy Display: Percent.
- Acceleration: Chill while learning, then Standard/Sport (Insane/Plaid on S/X).
- Stopping Mode: Hold (most regen), Creep, Roll.
- Steering Weight (Dynamics): Tesla recommends Standard. Trips: Energy > Trips or Controls > Trips; tire pressure: Controls > Service.

## 7. Model-specific
- Towing: Trailer Mode on; no Valet Mode.
- S/X: Controls > Suspension; lower saves energy.
- Cybertruck: Auto Lower (Controls > Dynamics) to Entry in Park.
- Controls by model year: tesla-model-differences.

Save to the profile. Sources: Tesla manuals (Collision Avoidance Assist, Lane Assist, Locks, Climate).

skills.name: tesla-towing-transport-mode
skills.description: Use when a Tesla needs to be towed, put on a flatbed, winched, or moved without driving: Transport Mode, Tow Mode, tow eye, free-rolling.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-towing-transport-mode
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla needs to be towed, put on a flatbed, winched, or moved
  without driving: Transport Mode, Tow Mode, tow eye, free-rolling.
---
Confirm model, year and trim first. Manuals call it Transport Mode or Tow Mode; quote that car's manual ("Instructions for Transporters"). Best first move: Roadside Assistance in the Tesla app.

## Key rule
- Tesla recommends a flatbed. Never tow with wheels on the ground: turning wheels make the motors generate power, which can overheat and damage the car.
- No flatbed: wheel lifts/dollies only with all four wheels off the ground, short distance (about 55 km / 35 mi in the manuals; check the car's manual).

## Turn on Transport / Tow Mode (car has power)
1. Car unplugged, key detected, low-voltage battery powered.
2. In Park, hold the brake, go to Controls > Service > Towing (Transport or Tow Mode by model/software).
3. Turn it on; the parking brake stays off for winching or pushing. Wheels may turn only under 3 mph (5 km/h), for less than 30 ft (10 m): winch onto a flatbed or move a short way only.
4. Rolling faster than 5 mph (8 km/h) cancels it and engages the parking brake. Exit by shifting into Park. Losing low-voltage power also ends it and applies the parking brake.

## Tow points
- 3/Y/S/X: tow eye in the frunk (or with the tire repair kit). Pop the front bumper cover, thread it counter-clockwise, tighten fully. For winching onto a flatbed only.
- Cybertruck: square tow hooks under the front fascia.
- Never strap to suspension parts; use the manual's approved points.

## No power
- Mode needs low-voltage power: try a jump first (tesla-lost-key-dead-battery).
- Otherwise the operator uses self-loading wheel dollies or tire skates so wheels don't turn; tell them it's an EV.

Trailer towing is different: capacity in tesla-model-differences; Trailer Mode, range and Supercharging in tesla-charging-and-road-trips.

Related: tesla-service-warranty-delivery (Roadside), tesla-troubleshooting.
Sources: Tesla owner's manuals (Instructions for Transporters; Transport/Tow Mode; Attaching the Tow Eye), tesla.com/roadside-assistance. Menu name and distance limit vary by manual.

skills.name: tesla-troubleshooting
skills.description: Use when something on a Tesla isn't working: won't start or unlock, app offline, phone key, charging, frozen screen while driving, warnings, Bluetooth, stuck update, service vs roadside.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-troubleshooting
description: >-
  Use when something on a Tesla isn't working: won't start or unlock, app
  offline, phone key, charging, frozen screen while driving, warnings,
  Bluetooth, stuck update, service vs roadside.
---
## If you're driving right now (screen black, frozen, or a warning)
Answer this first, before any profile questions.
1. **Turn on the hazard lights.** Keep both hands on the wheel and drive calmly.
2. **Pull over safely** when you can, and shift into **Park** (only if the screen won't let you shift: on 2024+ Model 3 and 2025+ Model Y, use the **overhead P/R/N/D buttons**).
3. **First fix: restart the touchscreen.** In Park, **hold both steering-wheel scroll buttons until the screen goes black**, then wait about 30 seconds for it to come back (full steps below). If it's still frozen, do a power off.
- Tesla says a touchscreen restart affects only the infotainment system (service.tesla.com), but restart only in Park: status, safety warnings and the backup camera aren't shown during it.
- **If steering or braking feels off, stop safely and call for help.** For smoke, fire, a crash, or a brake or steering fault, call **911** or Tesla Roadside in the app.

**Then confirm model, year, software** (tesla-model-differences). Locked out/dead car: **tesla-lost-key-dead-battery** first.
Rules: one step at a time. Reboot only in **Park**, never while driving. **Don't remove the phone key or unpair Bluetooth** without a working key card. Label guesses. Out of steps: **Section I**.

## Two resets
- **Touchscreen restart:** Park. **Hold both scroll buttons** (S/X, Cybertruck: scroll wheels) until black; ~**30 seconds**. 2024+ 3 / 2025+ Y: a *brief* press activates overhead P/R/N/D; hold to restart.
- **Power off:** Park, **Controls > Safety > Power Off**, wait **≥2 minutes** touching nothing; brake or door to wake.

## A. Won't start/shift, dark screen
1. Brake firmly. 2. Key card on console reader (works = phone key issue → C). 3. App **Controls > Start (Keyless Driving)**. 4. Frozen: restart, then power off. 5. 2024+ 3 / 2025+ Y can't shift: overhead P/R/N/D. 6. "Unable to drive"/"Vehicle may not restart": stop retrying; I. 7. **Totally dead:** tesla-lost-key-dead-battery. 8. **HV at 0%:** Roadside.

## B. App offline
1. Wake by door/brake. 2. **Controls > Safety > Allow Mobile Access** ON. 3. Phone: data, app updated, Bluetooth ON, Background App Refresh ON / battery optimization OFF, Location **Always**. 4. Sign out/in, reinstall. 5. Restart, power off 2+ min. 6. Carry a **key card**; request service.

## C. Phone key not detected
1. **Key card** on pillar. 2. Phone checks as in B. 3. Restart phone, then touchscreen. 4. Re-add only in the car with the card: Controls > Locks, remove phone key; app Set Up Phone Key, tap card. 5. All phones fail: service.

## D. Charging
1. Port light: **blinking green** charging; **solid green** complete; **solid amber** not seated; **blinking amber** reduced current; **solid red** fault.
2. Schedule or **limit**? Controls > Charging. 3. Home: reset breaker, lower amps. 4. Supercharger: reseat; **another stall** (not its 1A/1B pair). 5. **Cybertruck can't use CCS Combo 1**; adapter on cable *before* the car. 6. Cold: navigate to precondition. 7. Stuck cable: app Open Charge Port. 8. Faults everywhere: service.

## E. Screen frozen/laggy
Restart in Park only. Failing **Dashcam drive** causes lag (tesla-dashcam-sentry). Black while driving: see top; no screen = no warnings, wipers, defrost: urgent if it lasts.

## F. Alerts
**"Vehicle may not restart"/"Unable to drive":** urgent; consider Roadside. LV battery alert: book promptly. Details: tesla-service-mode-and-alerts.

## G. Bluetooth
**Priority** device, Media/Phone/Contacts on; restart screen; re-pair (card nearby if it's your key). No CarPlay/Android Auto.

## H. Update stuck
Park, strong Wi-Fi; **can't drive while installing**. **>~3 hours**: touchscreen restart. Still won't drive: service; must move it: Roadside.

## I. Service or Roadside?
- **Roadside** when it **can't be driven or is unsafe**: app **Service > Roadside Assistance** or **1-877-798-3752** (US/Canada, 24/7).
- **Book service** (Service > Request Service) when it drives safely; include photos and alert text.
- **Crash, fire, smoke, injury: 911 first.**

Sources: Tesla manuals (Restarting the Touchscreen, Troubleshooting Alerts), tesla.com/roadside-assistance.

skills.name: tesla-valet-mode
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner asks about Valet Mode: what it limits, turning it on or off from the touchscreen or app, the valet PIN, or handing the car to a valet or shop.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-valet-mode
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner asks about Valet Mode: what it limits, turning it on or
  off from the touchscreen or app, the valet PIN, or handing the car to a valet
  or shop.
---
Confirm model, year and software first (paths differ).

## What it restricts (current manuals)
- Speed capped at 70 mph (113 km/h); acceleration and power limited.
- Frunk and glovebox locked; Home and Work hidden in navigation.
- Voice, Self-Driving features, HomeLink, profiles, Toybox and Theater off; key list hidden; no new Wi-Fi/Bluetooth pairing.
- Key card: current Model Y and Cybertruck manuals say a key card must be used in Valet Mode; Model 3 (some regions) and Model X manuals don't say this.

## Turn on (touchscreen)
1. Park. 2. Controls > Safety > Valet Mode, or the driver profile icon > Valet Mode. 3. First time: create a 4-digit valet PIN. 4. Screen shows Valet.

## App
In Park, start or cancel in the Tesla app; no PIN needed.

## Turn off
- In Park, touch the Valet profile icon and enter the PIN; last profile and climate return.
- Forgot the PIN: reset in the car with your Tesla account credentials (also cancels Valet), or cancel from the app.

## With PIN to Drive and Glovebox PIN (manual)
- With PIN to Drive on, enter the driving PIN before creating or entering the valet PIN. The valet drives without the driving PIN.
- A Glovebox PIN still opens the glovebox in Valet Mode for you. See tesla-pin-to-drive.

Don't use while towing: torque limits can make hills hard (Tesla warning).

## Handing over (common sense)
Give a key card, not your phone; turn Valet on before arriving and check "Valet" shows; take valuables (rear trunk isn't locked); consider Sentry/Dashcam; ask service whether they need Valet off for a road test.

Sources: Tesla manuals (Valet Mode; PIN to Drive; Glovebox), checked Oct 2026.

skills.name: tesla-voice-commands
skills.description: Use when a Tesla owner wants a quick reference of voice commands, how to start a voice command, or how to talk to Grok in the car.
skills.content:
---
name: tesla-voice-commands
description: >-
  Use when a Tesla owner wants a quick reference of voice commands, how to start
  a voice command, or how to talk to Grok in the car.
---
From the manual's "Voice Commands" page and tesla.com/support/voice-commands unless marked; varies by model, region, software. Needs Standard Connectivity. No driving commands.

## Start a command
- Right scroll-wheel/mic button on the wheel or yoke (all models), or the touchscreen mic.
- Grok: press and hold the same button, App Launcher > Grok, or "Hey Grok" once enabled (support page: Controls > Audio > Grok Settings; recent notes: Grok > Settings). Say "goodbye" to end.
- Some commands Park-only.

## Examples
- Navigation: "Navigate home," "Show nearby Superchargers."
- Climate: "Set the temperature to 72," "I'm cold," seat heaters, "Turn on Pet Mode" (Park).
- Media: "Play [artist and song]," skip, volume (streaming needs Premium or Wi-Fi), "Open Netflix / YouTube" (Park only).
- Phone (Bluetooth): "Call…," "Text…" (needs message sync).
- Vehicle: wipers; "Open the glovebox"; "Keep my car safe" (Sentry); lock/unlock; charge port; "Show me the Owner's Manual."
- Dashcam: "Save Dashcam" is owner-reported, not on Tesla's list. Reliable: tap the Dashcam icon or On Honk.
- "Bug report" plus description in one sentence goes to Tesla; not a service request.

## Grok (canonical section)
- Requirements (tesla.com/support/grok): AMD infotainment processor, software 2025.26+, Premium Connectivity or Wi-Fi. Check Controls > Software > Additional Vehicle Information.
- 3, Y, S, X, Cybertruck with AMD Ryzen; country-dependent. Intel Atom cars (most built before about late 2021–2022) not eligible today; no timeline for more. Check the car, not the year.
- No Grok account or subscription needed to turn it on; signing in unlocks Connectors and your own limits.
- Owners report a standard X Premium subscription is enough for in-car Grok and that it does more than chat: connect Grok to their account, send it tasks, and check in with their Grok bots from the car. SuperGrok Heavy is not required for this.
- Can navigate, call, play music, adjust climate, answer car questions.
- Personalities in Grok settings; use Assistant for car commands. Connectors and Grok Bot need 2026.26+ and a signed-in account; features may vary by plan.
- Privacy: Grok conversations anonymous to Tesla, not tied to the car; standard voice transcriptions processed without audio, not linked to your account.
